title: Safekeys Encrypted Folder Manifest v1
description: The manifest.json of a Safekeys folder. A folder is an ordinary directory holding ciphertext blobs, this manifest, and a README.safekeys. Copying a folder increases no cryptographic exposure: it is inert without a live token AND a reachable sidecar AND a key authority. INVARIANT: the manifest is metadata only. It MUST NOT contain plaintext, an unwrapped DEK, or a KEK. additionalProperties is false so material cannot be smuggled in. Note that wrapped (envelope-encrypted) DEKs are permitted — they are useless without the KEK.

safekeys.description: Format version of this manifest. A resolver MUST refuse a version it does not implement rather than attempting best-effort parsing.

objects.description: The ciphertext objects in this folder. Objects are inert blobs; the manifest describes them but cannot decrypt them.

id.description: Object identifier. Referenced by a token's sid, and by token_references below.

path.description: Relative path to the ciphertext blob. MUST be under objects/ and MUST end in .enc — never an unencrypted file.

alg.description: AEAD algorithm used for this object. Both are permitted; AES-256-GCM is the FIPS-oriented choice, ChaCha20-Poly1305 the constant-time-in-software choice.

wrapped_key.description: Envelope-wrapped data encryption key (DEK). PERMITTED because it is wrapped: it is useless without the KEK, which never leaves the key store. This is the only key-shaped field allowed in a folder. Implementations SHOULD use their key store's native wrapped-key encoding (e.g. Vault transit 'vault:v1:…'), so the pattern permits base64 plus common separator characters.

wrapping_kid.description: Identifier of the KEK that wrapped this DEK. Enables rotation and multi-authority resolution. REQUIRED in practice once more than one KEK exists; optional only for single-KEK folders.

content_type.description: Hint describing the plaintext's media type, e.g. text/plain or application/x-pem-file. A hint only — implementations MUST NOT use it to decide whether to decrypt.

hash.description: Integrity hash of the ciphertext blob, as <algo>:<base64>, e.g. sha256:…. Optional; AEAD already provides integrity. Useful for sync and dedup.

size.description: Size of the ciphertext blob in bytes. Optional; a transport hint.

items.description: A safekey:// URI. Note this is a REFERENCE, not a live credential — a token embedded here is still subject to expiry, audience, and revocation at resolve time.

token_references.description: Optional references to tokens that may be used with this object. These are handles for discovery/auditing, never authority in themselves.

folder.description: Optional description of the folder as a whole, for multi-object folders.

id.description: Folder-level identifier, when the whole folder is treated as one transport unit.

description.description: A secret-free description of what this folder contains. Safe for model context.

authority.description: Optional pointer to the authority that can unwrap. A hint for operators; NOT a credential. Possessing this does not grant resolution.

issuer.description: Control plane issuer expected to mint tokens for this folder.

scope.description: Logical environment or tenant this folder belongs to.

$comment: Enforced by the implementation, NOT expressible in this schema: (1) every path in objects[].path MUST exist on disk and MUST be ciphertext; (2) no file outside objects/*.enc may be introduced; (3) README.safekeys MUST be present and MUST contain no secret material; (4) a 'wrapped_key' MUST NOT be unwrappable without the KEK — an implementation that finds an unwrapped DEK in a manifest MUST refuse to proceed and MUST log a security event.
